summary: Ephemeral CI-scoped API key provisioned to internal service after suspected credential-harvest form submission
description: Issue summary: Security team detected an ephemeral API key issued by our CI system that was used to access internal billing metadata and a staging-only service. The key creation timestamp correlates with a high-volume external form submission to a third-party survey provider. Impact: Potential short-lived access to internal endpoints and metadata. No confirmed data exfiltration yet. Action required: containment, audit, and improved detection.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) External form submission observed to service 'example-survey-provider.com' at 2026-03-12T09:12:30Z
2) CI webhook triggered a pipeline 'deploy-from-external-pr' which spins a runner and requests ephemeral credentials from internal token-service
3) Token-service issued a time-limited API key (scopes: ci:read, billing:metadata:read) to CI runner ID 'runner-17fc',
4) That API key was used to call /internal/billing/metadata and /staging/feature-toggle endpoints between 2026-03-12T09:13:05Z and 09:18:40Z
logs: token-service audit: 2026-03-12T09:13:01Z issued key id=ephemeral-3c9a scope=ci:read,billing:metadata:read issued_to=runner-17fc origin=ci-webhook
vault-audit: 2026-03-12T09:12:58Z token_request path=token-service/issue method=POST authenticated_service=ci-controller caller=runner-17fc
comments: 2026-03-12T09:25:00Z - Aisha Khan: Initial detection from platform-telemetry alert 'ephemeral-key-unusual-geo' fired. Observed single ephemeral key issued then used against internal endpoints. Escalating to Security and SRE.

2026-03-12T09:33:12Z - SRE - Daniel Wu: Confirmed api-gateway logs show LV (Latvia) geolocation which is unexpected for this CI runner. Runner mapping shows runner-17fc is usually eu-west; investigating runner assignment service.

2026-03-12T09:47:40Z - Security - Maya Patel: Blocking the source IP 35.212.44.9 at edge and revoking ephemeral-3c9a. Recommend rotating any long-lived tokens associated with pipeline service account 'ci-controller'.

2026-03-12T10:05:30Z - Platform Eng - Ravi Menon: Revoked ephemeral key id=ephemeral-3c9a via token-service revoke endpoint. Confirmed subsequent requests with that key return 401. Adding temporary rule to deny k=/internal/billing/* for ephemeral keys until scope review.

2026-03-12T11:20:05Z - Security - Maya Patel: Noted correlation between high-volume external form POSTs (extform-98ab) and webhook payloads to our CI webhook URL. Investigating whether the external form contains malicious JS or if credentials were captured by a customer-facing form and replayed by attacker. Open request to vendor to pull raw payloads.

2026-03-12T13:02:00Z - SRE - Daniel Wu: We've quarantined runner-17fc images and disabled auto-provisioning temporarily for pipelines triggered by external webhooks. Creating detection: if token-service issues keys with unexpected geolocation in <5min window, create Sev1 alert.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: User-submitted form contained JS that captured a webhook secret or user token and replayed it to trigger CI pipeline. Evidence: multiple recent external form submissions with referer header pointing to survey provider and similar payload shape.

Hypothesis 2: Malicious actor automated submissions to the external form, causing CI to provision runners that request ephemeral keys; runner images may have been compromised or misconfigured to use different egress IPs.
Query run: gcloud logging read 'resource.type="api_gateway" AND jsonPayload.keyId="ephemeral-3c9a"' --limit 50 returned 4 hits between 09:13 and 09:18 UTC

Vault audit review: token-service logged request from authenticated_service=ci-controller; need to validate whether pipeline used correct OIDC claims. OIDC token issuance timestamps align with pipeline trigger times.
SAML/SSO check: No suspicious interactive logins observed for ci-controller service account. No long-lived access keys appear in Vault for ci-controller except for standard read-only tokens.

Risk assessment: Scoped ephemeral key limited to read-only billing metadata and CI read; nonetheless access to billing metadata could expose customer billing identifiers and usage patterns. Treat as potential data exposure until cleared.
Telemetry gap: No existing rule to flag ephemeral key issuance with geo mismatch vs expected runner assignment. Added detection backlog item.
Potential false positive indicators: Some third-party CI runners legitimately egress from varied IPs; need to cross-check runner allocation logs.
resolution: Containment: revoked ephemeral key id=ephemeral-3c9a, blocked src IP 35.212.44.9, temporarily disabled external webhook-triggered pipelines, quarantined runner image. Remediation: rotated ci-controller long-lived tokens, added a policy to token-service to reject key issuance for requests with geolocation mismatch, created detection rule 'ephemeral-key-unexpected-geo', and updated CI webhook runbook with validation steps (verify HMAC secret and payload schema). Follow-up: Security to request payloads from external survey vendor, SRE to implement runner provenance checks, and Product to evaluate whether external webhook feature needs additional user-facing warnings. Ticket status: In Progress — follow-up work tracked in INT-947613 (runbook update) and SEC-1245 (detection engineering).
next_steps: 1) Security - request raw payloads from example-survey-provider and correlate IPs and headers (owner: Maya Patel, due: 2026-03-14)
2) SRE - implement runner provenance check and block if mismatch (owner: Daniel Wu, due: 2026-03-18)
3) Platform - add HMAC verification and stricter validation to external webhook endpoint (owner: Ravi Menon, due: 2026-03-17)
4) Detection - implement rule in platform-telemetry to alert on ephemeral key issuance with geo mismatch and automated revocation policy (owner: Security Detect Eng, due: 2026-03-16)
5) Post-incident: schedule tabletop to review webhook exposure model and update external integrations guidance (owner: Maya Patel, due: 2026-03-24)
